title: Temperance Lloyd Executed at Bideford: Last Witchcraft Execution in England
description: Temperance Lloyd was hanged at Exeter on August 25, 1682, along with Mary Trembles and Susanna Edwards from Bideford in Devon, in what were the last executions for witchcraft in England. Lloyd, an elderly poor woman with a long history of witch accusation, had been tried and acquitted previously before being convicted in 1682. All three women confessed, but their confessions were confused and incoherent in ways that troubled observers — one account noted that Lloyd claimed to have made a pact with the devil but could not remember what she had received in return. The Bideford executions proceeded despite skepticism from the trial judge and attracted significant commentary as an anachronism even at the time.
historiographical_note: Jonathan Barry's Witchcraft and Demonology in South-West England 1640–1789 (2012) provides the fullest modern account of the Bideford trials. The executions are significant for being both the last English witchcraft executions and an illustration of how prosecution could persist in provincial localities despite the erosion of elite credence. The judge's reluctance and the public commentary on the anachronism show how far elite opinion had shifted from the 1640s.
source_method: Contemporary pamphlet accounts; Exeter assize records; Barry, Witchcraft and Demonology in South-West England (2012)
